A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DextER and contain complete main texts and supplements. Text, equations, tables, figures, and relocated appendix material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original grasp-generation experiments on DexGYS and Dexonomy, including ablations, generalization, steering, and contact-prediction results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds backbone comparisons, simulated sensing robustness, inference timings, and failure-analysis results.

M1.justification: The proposed contact-then-grasp generation procedure, tokenization, hybrid attention, training objective, dropout, and steering mechanism remain unchanged. Alternative backbones are evaluated as ablations; the default architecture is retained.

E1.justification: DexGYS and Dexonomy coverage is retained. Appendix A.5 adds a distinct sensing scenario: partially observed, noisy point clouds generated from two simulated camera viewpoints. No new dataset or physical-robot evaluation is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Qwen2.5-1.5B and SmolLM2-360M as backbone comparison variants against the default Qwen2.5-0.5B. The established grasp-method comparator sets in Tables 1 and 3 remain unchanged; the timing comparison reuses existing comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include alternative backbone configurations, inference timing on one A6000 GPU, and zero-shot testing with HPR visibility filtering, approximately 35% retained points, and specified depth/lateral noise. Existing splits, training budgets, and grasp metrics remain unchanged; metric definitions are relocated to Appendix A.4.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens diagnostic evaluation with backbone-size/architecture ablations, partial-and-noisy observation robustness, inference-cost comparisons, and quantified penetration failures. These address capacity dependence, sensing assumptions, and execution weaknesses beyond v1's analyses. Unseen-taxonomy instability itself was already reported in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained standard deviations measure grasp diversity, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, steering, and contact-quality values remain unchanged. Added results include 67.55% and 64.87% success for the alternative backbones; 65.77% under partial/noisy inputs versus 67.14% with full observations; timings of 1.458 s for DextER, 1.105 s without ER, and 1.134 s for DexGYSNet; and penetration-related quantization failures comprising 14.7% of failures.

T1.justification: The probability factorization in Equation 1 and the contact/token representations are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: contact-based embodied reasoning, dataset annotations, and steerable grasp generation. The headline 67.14% success rate and 96.4% intention-alignment improvement are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning P-FID versus CD and mode coverage, backbone dependence, quantization-induced penetration, and missing stability cues for unseen taxonomies. Appendices expand annotation-design arguments and steering applications. The conclusion explicitly identifies simulation-only evaluation while qualifying the sensing limitation with the new robustness evidence.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports approximately 48 hours of training, clarifies collision-query contact annotation and the absence of geometric post-processing, and documents the sensing perturbations and timing hardware. These additions improve disclosure without establishing changes to the retained training procedure or annotation pipeline.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SmolLM2 and the Hidden Point Removal algorithm. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous grasp-generation and embodied-reasoning approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Selected introduction and method passages are rewritten, split descriptions are condensed, and Section 4.6 becomes Additional Analysis. Metric definitions move to the appendix, supplementary sections receive lettered numbering, and new analysis subsections are integrated without restructuring the overall argument.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Table 2 gains a backbone block, and new timing and robustness tables and a sensing illustration are added. Appendix illustrations are relocated or resized, several raster figures become sharper, and Figure 3's caption corrects rows to columns. Existing qualitative examples and prompts are retained.

improvement.justification: The backbone, sensing-robustness, and timing experiments address specific validation gaps in v1, while failure analysis and implementation disclosures clarify practical limitations. These provide a supported but limited improvement: the central results remain unchanged, robustness is tested synthetically, and the new findings lack uncertainty reporting.
